text:
sara_support: FYI customer ACME (#4521) reports sudden p99 regressions on /v1/realtime starting ~03:10 UTC. p50 ~200ms, p95 ~800ms, p99 spiking to ~3.2s and some timeouts. sample request_id=r-0a1b2c3 :frowning:

sara_support: Repro curl they sent (sanitized):
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/realtime \
  -d '{"input":"summarize: ...","model":"rwd/gpt-large"}' \n  -H 'x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3'
```

sara_support: They also attached a trace span that shows long queuing before worker started processing. Asking for triage and short-term mitigation.

raj_oncall: @sara_support thanks — is this tenant-only (ACME) or across tenants? any signs of a release/deploy around 03:00-03:15 UTC? :eyes:

lin_runtime: grabbing metrics now. Initial look: worker_pool.realtime-main.queue_depth for region-us-west jumped from ~8 -> ~90 at 03:10, sustained ~60 for ~5m. admission_rejects and queue_time/percentiles both increase.

mike_sre: I can confirm cluster-level autoscale didn’t kick immediately — scale headroom exhausted for that pool. metric excerpt: 
```
timestamp, queue_depth, running_replicas
03:05, 9, 12
03:10, 92, 12
03:12, 68, 12
03:18, 12, 18
```

mike_sre: looks like request pileup (spillover) — workers busy serving long sequences, admission window too tight, concurrency limit per-tenant is low.

lin_runtime: quick checks:
- model rwd/gpt-large avg seq len jumped for ACME from 420 -> 980 tokens around same time (customer traffic change)
- KV cache hit rate dropped (more unique prompts)

raj_oncall: short-term mitigations we can try now: increase tenant concurrency cap, enable temporary priority routing for ACME, and enable fallback thin model for latency-sensitive routes. Anyone can run control-plane change?

lin_runtime: I can do the config bump. Applying: 
```bash
# increase concurrency cap for tenant acme
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer INT-MGMT' \
  -d '{"max_concurrency":120}'

# enable routing rule: if processing_queue_ms > 800 => route to rwd/gpt-medium-fallback
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routes \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer INT-MGMT' \
  -d '{"match":{"tenant":"acme","path":"/v1/realtime"},"action":{"route_to":"rwd/gpt-medium-fallback","priority":100}}'
```

lin_runtime: applied both changes at 03:22 UTC.

deploy-bot: [deploy] routing-rule/v1 created by lin_runtime at 2026-03-17T03:22:14Z

mike_sre: after changes queue_depth dropped to ~15 and p99 latency fell to ~420ms within ~3m. Good short-term.

raj_oncall: Nice. Can we also enable softer admission (longer wait window) so small requests don't get rejected while large ones drain? And add a throttling policy that prioritizes requests < 300 tokens?

lin_runtime: added a fairness window + short-request priority rule:
```json
{"admission_policy":{"fairness_window_ms":800,"priority_rules":[{"max_tokens":300,"weight":10}]}}
```
(rolled at 03:26 UTC)

sara_support: I told ACME we've applied temporary settings and saw improvement. They want ETA for permanent fix and whether this will recur.

mike_sre: follow-ups:
- need to tune autoscaler to react faster for this pool (lower scale.cooldown, add predictive spike margin)
- consider separate dedicated pool for heavy ACME workloads or a reserved concurrency contract
- add alert for queue_depth > 50 AND kv_cache_hit < 30% to catch this pattern earlier

lin_runtime: I'll open infra ticket for autoscale tuning and a capacity recommendation doc for ACME. Drafting a post-incident note with graphs.

raj_oncall: TODOs:
- lin_runtime: run load replay for ACME trace to validate fallback quality (assigning)
- mike_sre: autoscaler tuning ticket + alert rule (assigning)
- sara_support: follow up with ACME on workload patterns and recommend model variant or Dedicated option

sara_support: ack, I'll schedule customer call. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lin_runtime: quick repro instructions for engineering:
```bash
# replay sample trace to reproduce Q buildup locally:
python infra/tools/replay.py --trace r-0a1b2c3 --rate 200 --region us-west --model rwd/gpt-large
```

mike_sre: adding note — avoid permanently raising tenant concurrency without capacity plan; this was a targeted short-term mitigation to relieve backlog. Long-term may need dedicated pool or quota purchase.

raj_oncall: closing loop here. If we see another spike, escalate to oncall pager and start emergency autoscale playbook.

sara_support: closing for now; will reopen thread if ACME reports recurrence. Thanks everyone.
